title: AhSilence: the open-source app that fights noise with more noise

facts.method: repo README, SUPPORT.md FAQ and GitHub API numbers, all fetched 2026-11-09
facts.limits: Single-tone cancellation only; the author admits in the FAQ that it is not perfect.

verify_before_render: Every point cites its source in the feature sheet (features.json evidence quotes).
Numbers on screen are the verified ones: 7-second scan, 4,876 stars, ±5° around 180°.

scenes.heading: HOW DO HEADPHONES SILENCE A SCREAMING PLATFORM?
scenes.say: How do noise cancelling headphones buy you silence on a screaming platform? They pour even more sound into your ears. Every hum is a wave of air, pushing and pulling.

scenes.heading: COPY IT. FLIP IT.
scenes.say: Play an exact copy upside down at the same moment, and the two flatten into silence.

scenes.heading: ONE APP DOES IT ON YOUR PHONE
scenes.say: One developer packed that trick into an Android app for your phone. AhSilence.

scenes.heading: SEVEN SECONDS OF LISTENING
scenes.say: It listens to your room for seven seconds and picks out the strongest drone.

scenes.heading: PLAYED BACK UPSIDE DOWN
scenes.say: Then it plays that hum back, upside down.

scenes.heading: EXACT, OR TWICE AS LOUD
scenes.say: The timing has to be exact. A hum repeats every sixteen milliseconds. Half a cycle late, and you double it.

scenes.heading: STEADY HUMS YES, VOICES NO
scenes.say: That is why it chases steady hums, like an air conditioner, and leaves voices alone.

scenes.heading: BLUETOOTH DELAY? TRIM IT BY HAND
nodes: five degrees around one hundred eighty
scenes.say: Bluetooth adds delay, so the app gives you a phase dial: small turns, about five degrees, around one hundred eighty.

scenes.heading: THE AUTHOR ADMITS IT
scenes.say: The author admits it in the FAQ: the cancellation isn't perfect.

scenes.heading: NOISE vs NOISE
scenes.say: Same trick as the headphones. Fighting noise with more noise.
Follow for more. Comment ahsilence for the repo link.

idea: AhSilence listens to a steady hum for seven seconds, finds the dominant tone, then plays the same wave flipped 180 degrees through the headphones so the hum erases itself - and the author admits in the FAQ that the cancellation is not perfect.

claims.text: AhSilence generates phase-inverted anti-noise that cancels steady drones (engine or fan hum), not voices.
It listens for seven seconds first: 16-bit PCM at 44.1 kHz, measuring which single tone is the strongest.
A phase calibrator dial (0-360 degrees) lets you correct bluetooth delay by hand until the hum fades.
The app is free, offline, Kotlin, Apache-2.0, ~4,876 stars at fetch time.
The author's own FAQ says: 'The cancellation isn't perfect. What can I do?'
